Base Account — Comprehensive LLM-Friendly Reference (Plain Text)
================================================================

Source: Collated and normalized from Base Account docs. This file contains API methods & signatures, type/interface definitions, configuration options, code examples, provider RPC methods, capabilities, SDK utilities, UI components, integration guides, error handling, troubleshooting tips, and best practices. Use for training or retrieval contexts.

High-level overview
-------------------
- Base Account: smart-wallet-backed account layer (ERC-4337 smart wallets) that provides universal sign-in, Base Pay (one-tap USDC), profile/data callback support, sub-accounts, spend permissions, sponsor/gas paymaster support, batch transactions, cross-chain support.
- Primary integration point: Base Account SDK (createBaseAccountSDK) which exposes an EIP-1193 compliant provider plus SDK helpers (subAccount manager, utilities).
- Provider.request handles calls in three ways:
  1. Sent to Wallet UI / Popup / Mobile app (for interactive actions).
  2. Handled locally by SDK (some read-only or stateful methods).
  3. Forwarded to configured RPC transport for blockchain queries.

SDK: createBaseAccountSDK (entrypoint)
-------------------------------------
Signature:
```ts
function createBaseAccountSDK(options?: CreateProviderOptions): BaseAccountSDK
```

CreateProviderOptions (shape)
- appName?: string
- appLogoUrl?: string
- appChainIds?: number[]             // list of chain IDs your app supports
- preference?: Preference
  - walletUrl?: string               // override default wallet URL (advanced)
  - attribution?: { auto?: boolean; dataSuffix?: `0x${string}` }
  - telemetry?: boolean
- subAccounts?: Omit<SubAccountOptions, 'enableAutoSubAccounts'>
  - toOwnerAccount?: ToOwnerAccountFn
- paymasterUrls?: Record<number, string> // chainId -> paymaster URL
- telemetry default: true

Return: BaseAccountSDK
- getProvider(): ProviderInterface (EIP-1193 provider)
- subAccount: {
    create(account: AddSubAccountAccount): Promise<SubAccount>;
    get(): Promise<SubAccount | null>;
    addOwner(params: { address?: `0x${string}`; publicKey?: `0x${string}`; chainId: number }): Promise<string>;
    setToOwnerAccount(fn: ToOwnerAccountFn): void;
  }
- Other helpers exposed by SDK: generateKeyPair, getKeypair, getCryptoKeyAccount, pay helpers (pay, getPaymentStatus), spend-permission helpers, etc.

Core types & interfaces (concise)
---------------------------------
(TypeScript-like pseudotypes for LLM consumption.)

ProviderInterface (EIP-1193)
```ts
interface RequestArguments {
  method: string;
  params?: unknown[] | object;
}

interface ProviderRpcError extends Error {
  message: string;
  code: number;
  data?: unknown;
}

interface ProviderInterface {
  request(args: RequestArguments): Promise<unknown>;
  disconnect(): Promise<void>;
  on(event: 'connect' | 'disconnect' | 'accountsChanged' | 'chainChanged', listener: (payload:any)=>void): this;
  emit(event: string, payload?: any): boolean;
}
```

CreateProviderOptions (expanded)
```ts
type CreateProviderOptions = {
  appName?: string;
  appLogoUrl?: string;
  appChainIds?: number[];
  preference?: {
    walletUrl?: string;
    attribution?: { auto?: boolean; dataSuffix?: `0x${string}` };
    telemetry?: boolean;
  };
  subAccounts?: {
    toOwnerAccount?: () => Promise<{ account: OwnerAccount | null }>;
  };
  paymasterUrls?: Record<number, string>;
};
```

OwnerAccount union used by subAccounts:
- LocalAccount (viem)
- WebAuthnAccount (webauthn-based account)
- Any viem-compatible account representation

SubAccount shape
```ts
type SubAccount = {
  address: `0x${string}`;
  factory?: `0x${string}`;
  factoryData?: `0x${string}`;
}
```

SpendPermission (SDK representation)
```ts
type SpendPermission = {
  permissionHash: string; // EIP-712 hash
  signature: string;
  chainId: number;
  permission: {
    account: string;
    spender: string;
    token: string;
    allowance: bigint;
    period: number; // seconds
    start: number; // unix seconds
    end: number;   // unix seconds
    salt: string;  // hex
    extraData: string; // hex bytes
  }
}
```

Payment / Base Pay types
```ts
type PayOptions = {
  amount: string; // USD string like "10.50"
  to: string; // 0x address or ENS
  testnet?: boolean; // default false
  payerInfo?: {
    requests: Array<{ type: 'email'|'name'|'phoneNumber'|'physicalAddress'|'onchainAddress'; optional?: boolean }>;
    callbackURL?: string;
  }
}
type PayResult = {
  id: string; // tx id / payment id
  amount: string;
  to: string;
  payerInfoResponses?: any;
}
type PaymentStatus = { status: 'completed'|'pending'|'failed'|'not_found'; id: string; message?: string; sender?: string; amount?: string; recipient?: string; error?: string }
```

Key utilities
- generateKeyPair(): Promise<P256KeyPair>
- getKeypair(): Promise<P256KeyPair | null>
- getCryptoKeyAccount(): Promise<{ account: WebAuthnAccount | LocalAccount | null }>

Core SDK utilities signatures
-----------------------------
- createBaseAccountSDK(options?: CreateProviderOptions): BaseAccountSDK
- generateKeyPair(): Promise<{ publicKey: string; privateKey: string }>
- getKeypair(): Promise<{ publicKey: string; privateKey: string } | null>
- getCryptoKeyAccount(): Promise<{ account: WebAuthnAccount | LocalAccount | null }>

Provider: getProvider() usage
-----------------------------
- provider.request({ method: 'eth_requestAccounts' }) -> Promise<string[]>
- provider.request({ method: 'wallet_connect', params: [options] }) -> Promise<{ accounts: AccountResult[], chainId: string, isConnected: boolean }>
- provider.request({ method: 'wallet_sendCalls', params: [callBundle] }) -> Promise<callsId | result>
- provider.request({ method: 'wallet_getCapabilities', params: [address] }) -> Promise<CapabilitiesObject>
- provider emits events: 'accountsChanged', 'chainChanged', 'connect', 'disconnect'

Core flows: Sign In (SIWE) and wallet_connect
--------------------------------------------
- Use wallet_connect with capability signInWithEthereum to get an address and a signed SIWE message and signature.
- Always generate a fresh nonce (crypto.randomUUID or server-supplied) for SIWE to prevent replay.
- Verify on backend with viem verifyMessage or similar.

Example (SIWE with provider):
```ts
const nonce = window.crypto.randomUUID().replace(/-/g,'');
const res = await provider.request({
  method: 'wallet_connect',
  params: [{
    version: '1',
    capabilities: {
      signInWithEthereum: { nonce, chainId: '0x2105' }
    }
  }]
});
const accounts = res.accounts;
const address = accounts[0].address;
const { message, signature } = accounts[0].capabilities.signInWithEthereum;
// send to backend for verification
```

Backend verification (viem)
```ts
import { createPublicClient, http } from 'viem';
import { base } from 'viem/chains';
const client = createPublicClient({ chain: base, transport: http() });
const valid = await client.verifyMessage({ address, message, signature });
```

Payments: pay() & getPaymentStatus()
-----------------------------------
SDK functions:
- pay(options: PayOptions): Promise<PayResult>
- getPaymentStatus({id: string, testnet?: boolean}): Promise<PaymentStatus>

Behavior:
- pay() triggers wallet popup, handles USDC conversion and gas/payer flow.
- getPaymentStatus must be called with the same testnet flag used for pay().

Examples:
Basic:
```ts
import { pay, getPaymentStatus } from '@base-org/account';
try {
  const result = await pay({ amount: '5.00', to: '0xRecipient', testnet: true });
  const status = await getPaymentStatus({ id: result.id, testnet: true });
} catch (err) { console.error(err); }
```

Collecting payer info (dataCallback):
- pass payerInfo.requests and optional callbackURL
- If callbackURL provided, wallet POSTs collected data to that endpoint for validation. Your API must return either { request: { ...calls... } } (success) or { errors: { ... } } (validation errors) exactly per docs.

DataCallback request body shape (sent to callbackURL)
```json
{
  "calls": [{ "to": "...", "data": "0x..." }, ...],
  "chainId": "0x14a34",
  "capabilities": {
    "dataCallback": {
      "requestedInfo": {
        "email": "user@example.com",
        "phoneNumber": { "number": "+12...", "country": "US", "isPrimary": true },
        "physicalAddress": { "address1":"...", "city":"...", "postalCode":"...", "countryCode":"US", "name":{ "firstName":"", "familyName":"" } },
        "name": { "firstName":"", "familyName":"" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Expected callback success response:
```json
{ "request": { "calls": [...], "chainId": "...", "capabilities": { dataCallback: { ... } } } }
```
Or validation errors:
```json
{ "errors": { "email": "Invalid", "physicalAddress": { "postalCode":"Invalid" } } }
```

BasePayButton UI component
--------------------------
Package: @base-org/account-ui/react

Props (summary):
- paymentOptions: PayOptions (required)
- colorScheme?: 'light'|'dark'|'system'
- size?: 'small'|'medium'|'large'
- variant?: 'solid'|'outline'
- disabled?: boolean
- onPaymentResult?: (result: { success: boolean; transactionHash?: string; error?: string; payerInfoResponses?: any }) => void
- onClick?: () => boolean | void (return false to cancel payment)

Example:
```tsx
<BasePayButton
  paymentOptions={{ amount: '25.00', to: 'merchant.eth', payerInfo: { requests: [ {type:'email'} ], callbackURL: 'https://your-api.com/validate' } }}
  colorScheme="light"
  onPaymentResult={(res) => { if (res.success) console.log('done'); }}
/>
```

Authentication UI: SignInWithBaseButton
--------------------------------------
Package: @base-org/account-ui/react

Props:
- align?: 'left'|'center'|'right'
- variant?: 'solid'|'transparent'
- colorScheme?: 'light'|'dark'|'system'
- size?: 'small'|'medium'|'large'
- disabled?: boolean
- onClick?: () => void
- onSignInResult?: (result) => void

Example usage:
```tsx
<SignInWithBaseButton onClick={async () => { /* run wallet_connect SIWE flow */ }} />
```

Provider RPC methods (complete list & shapes)
---------------------------------------------
Provider.request expects { method: string, params?: any[] | object }.

Categories:
1. Sent to Wallet / interactive (handled by wallet app / popup)
   - personal_sign
   - eth_sendTransaction
   - eth_sendRawTransaction
   - eth_signTypedData_v4
   - wallet_addEthereumChain
   - wallet_watchAsset
   - wallet_sendCalls
   - wallet_getCallsStatus
   - wallet_connect
   - wallet_getCapabilities
   - wallet_switchEthereumChain
   - wallet_addSubAccount
   - wallet_getSubAccounts
   - coinbase_fetchPermissions

2. Handled locally by SDK
   - eth_requestAccounts
   - eth_accounts
   - eth_coinbase
   - eth_chainId
   - web3_clientVersion

3. Passed to RPC provider
   - eth_getBalance, eth_blockNumber, eth_gasPrice, eth_estimateGas, eth_feeHistory, eth_getBlockByNumber, eth_getBlockByHash, eth_getTransactionByHash, eth_getTransactionReceipt, eth_getTransactionCount, eth_getTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex, eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex, eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash, eth_getBlockTransactionCountByNumber, eth_getCode, eth_getStorageAt, eth_getLogs, eth_getProof, eth_getUncleCountByBlockHash, eth_getUncleCountByBlockNumber, eth_sendRawTransaction

Selected request/response examples (representative)
- eth_requestAccounts -> returns string[] of addresses or throws 4001 if user rejects.
- wallet_connect -> format (see SIWE example above).
- wallet_getCapabilities params: [accountAddress], returns mapping chainId -> capabilities object:
  - capabilities keys: auxiliaryFunds, atomic, paymasterService, flowControl, datacallback
- wallet_sendCalls params: [ { version: '2.0.0', id?: string, from: '0x..', chainId: '0x...', atomicRequired: boolean, calls: [ { to, value, data } ], capabilities?: {...} } ]
  - returns batchId / callsId; caller can call wallet_getCallsStatus(callsId) to poll receipts/status
- wallet_getCallsStatus params: [callsId] returns { version, chainId, id, status: number, atomic: boolean, receipts: [...] } (see docs for codes: 100 pending, 200 success, 4xx offchain failure, 5xx chain failure, 6xx partial failure)

Capabilities (detailed)
-----------------------

Capabilities are discovered via wallet_getCapabilities(account). They are chain-specific.

Common capability keys:
- signInWithEthereum (used with wallet_connect)
  - params: { nonce: string, chainId: string }
  - returns message & signature
- auxiliaryFunds
  - indicates wallet may have access to off-chain/auxiliary funds (MagicSpend)
  - properties: { supported: boolean }
  - App behavioral impact: do not block actions solely because on-chain balance is zero when auxiliaryFunds.supported === true
- atomic
  - values: { supported: 'supported' | 'ready' | 'unsupported' }
  - 'ready' means EOA can upgrade to atomic support with user approval
- paymasterService
  - used to request sponsorship from an ERC-7677 paymaster web service
  - params: { url: 'https://..' }
  - returns paymaster support boolean
- dataCallback (data collection during payments)
  - used for payerInfo collection (email, name, phoneNumber, physicalAddress, onchainAddress)
  - app supplies callbackURL optionally; wallet posts to your URL for server-side validation
- flowControl (ERC-7867 proposed)
  - controls behavior on failure inside batched calls (onFailure: 'continue'|'stop'|'retry', fallbackCall etc.)

Batch transactions: wallet_sendCalls (EIP-5792)
-----------------------------------------------
- Use wallet_sendCalls to submit multiple onchain calls in a single flow.
- version: '2.0.0'
- atomicRequired: true => request atomic execution (all succeed or all revert). Must check wallet_getCapabilities().atomic.
- Non-atomic mode allowed: atomicRequired: false -> wallet might run in sequence and some calls could succeed even if some fail.
- Use encodeFunctionData/ABI to construct data fields for contract calls (viem/ethers).

Example: simple batch ETH transfers
```ts
const calls = [
  { to: addr1, value: numberToHex(parseEther('0.001')), data: '0x' },
  { to: addr2, value: numberToHex(parseEther('0.001')), data: '0x' }
];
const result = await provider.request({
  method: 'wallet_sendCalls',
  params: [{
    version: '2.0.0',
    from: fromAddress,
    chainId: numberToHex(base.constants.CHAIN_IDS.base),
    atomicRequired: true,
    calls
  }]
});
```

Error handling for wallet_sendCalls (common codes):
- 4001: user rejected
- 5740: batch too large for wallet
- -32602: invalid params
- 5700: required capability not supported

Spend Permissions (overview & SDK helpers)
-----------------------------------------
Spend Permissions let apps request user-signed EIP-712 spend permissions that a "spender" can later use to move tokens from the user's Base Account within configured limits. Useful for subscriptions, automated payouts, etc.

Key SDK methods (signatures & behavior):
- requestSpendPermission({ account, spender, token, chainId, allowance: bigint, periodInDays, start?: Date, end?: Date, salt?: string, extraData?: string, provider }): Promise<SpendPermission>
  - prompts user to sign EIP-712 permission
- fetchPermissions({ account, chainId, spender, provider }): Promise<SpendPermission[]>
  - returns active, non-revoked permissions for spender
- getPermissionStatus(permission): Promise<{ isActive: boolean; remainingSpend: bigint; nextPeriodStart: Date }>
- prepareSpendCallData({ permission, amount?: bigint }): Promise<Call[]>
  - returns one or two Call objects:
    - If permission not yet registered: approveWithSignature call followed by spend call
    - If already registered: only spend call
- requestRevoke(permission): Promise<string> (tx hash)
  - triggers wallet flow to revoke permission (user interaction)
- prepareRevokeCallData(permission): Promise<Call>
  - returns call data your spender can submit silently (on-chain revoke) without user interaction

Spend permission flow example:
1. requestSpendPermission(...) -> returns permission with signature.
2. prepareSpendCallData({permission, amount}) -> returns calls.
3. Spender account submits calls as batch (wallet_sendCalls) or sequential (eth_sendTransaction).

Sub Accounts (overview)
-----------------------
Sub Accounts are child accounts created/managed under a Base Account to reduce passkey prompts and provide app-specific accounts.

RPCs:
- wallet_addSubAccount params: { account: { type: 'create'|'deployed', keys?: [], address?: '0x..', chainId?: number } } -> returns { address, factory?, factoryData? }
- wallet_getSubAccounts params: { account: '0x..', domain: 'https://app.yourdomain' } -> returns { subAccounts: [ ... ] }

SDK conveniences:
- sdk.subAccount.create() // wraps wallet_addSubAccount
- sdk.subAccount.get()
- sdk.subAccount.addOwner({ address, publicKey, chainId })
- sdk.subAccount.setToOwnerAccount(fn) // set owner account (embedded/local wallet) for signing sub-account transactions

Typical sub-account steps (Privy example):
1. Provide embedded wallet (Privy) as owner.
2. Call wallet_addSubAccount to create or import sub account.
3. Configure toOwnerAccount for signing.

Sub Account transaction usage:
- Once subaccount is created, use wallet_sendCalls or eth_sendTransaction where from == subAccount.address. The provider will route signing to the configured owner account (embedded wallet) and avoid passkey prompts.

Basenames (ENS-based)
---------------------
- Basenames are ENS-like onchain names for Base network.
- To resolve Basename for an address: call L2 resolver contract read name(reverseNode).
- To fetch text records/avatar: use resolver ABI L2ResolverAbi and query text records by keys.
- Implementation notes:
  - convertReverseNodeToBytes(address, chainId) used to compute reverse node bytes for resolver.
  - Basename metadata stored as text records.

OnchainKit & Wagmi Basename resolver examples:
- See code examples in docs: create ABI file abis/L2ResolverAbi.ts (use provided gist), query contract using viem public client or wagmi.

Wagmi integration examples
--------------------------
Wagmi config examples (connectors, transports, chain config):

Example wagmi.ts:
```ts
import { http, cookieStorage, createConfig, createStorage } from 'wagmi';
import { base, baseSepolia } from 'wagmi/chains';
import { coinbaseWallet, injected } from 'wagmi/connectors';

export function getConfig() {
  return createConfig({
    chains: [base, baseSepolia],
    connectors: [
      injected(),
      coinbaseWallet({ appName: 'Create Wagmi', preference: 'smartWalletOnly' }),
    ],
    storage: createStorage({ storage: cookieStorage }),
    ssr: true,
    transports: {
      [base.id]: http(),
      [baseSepolia.id]: http(),
    },
  });
}
```

Using Base Account connector in Wagmi:
- Find connector connectors.find(c => c.id === 'baseAccountWallet') then connectAsync({ connector: baseAccountConnector })
- Access provider via connector.provider for advanced RPC methods.

Wagmi Sign-in with Base flow (summary):
1. connectAsync({ connector: baseAccountConnector })
2. provider = baseAccountConnector.provider
3. provider.request({ method: 'wallet_connect', params: [{ version: '1', capabilities:{ signInWithEthereum: { nonce, chainId } } }] })
4. Backend verify signature with viem

Privy integration
-----------------
Privy + Base Account steps:
- Install: @privy-io/react-auth @privy-io/wagmi-connector wagmi viem @base-org/account
- Provide PrivyProvider wrapping WagmiProvider with wagmi config including baseAccount connector
- Privy hooks provide embeddedWallet and baseAccountWallet references and baseAccountSdk via useBaseAccountSdk
- Examples: wallet linking, creating Sub Accounts with embedded wallet as owner via baseAccountSdk.subAccount.setToOwnerAccount(toViemAccount)

Mobile integration (React Native) — Mobile Wallet Protocol Client
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Use @mobile-wallet-protocol/client and polyfills (expo-standard-web-crypto, react-native-url-polyfill)
- Create EIP1193Provider with metadata { name, customScheme: 'myapp://', chainIds: [8453], logoUrl }
- Or use @mobile-wallet-protocol/wagmi-connectors to create a wagmi connector for CoinbaseSmartWallet / Base Account

Paymasters and sponsor gas
--------------------------
- Base Account supports ERC-7677 paymaster-based sponsorship.
- Setup:
  1. Obtain paymaster service URL (Coinbase Developer Platform recommended).
  2. Configure app/paymaster allowlist and optionally set policy (Coinbase Developer Platform supports).
  3. In provider request wallet_sendCalls include capabilities: { paymasterService: { url: paymasterServiceUrl } }.
- Also supports ERC20-based paymasters (special ERC20 paymaster flow). For ERC20 paymasters, app must ensure token approvals to paymaster address (allowance top-ups).
- Paymaster RPC endpoints to implement (pm_getPaymasterStubData / pm_getPaymasterData) and pm_getAcceptedPaymentTokens as per ERC-7677.

Paymaster example (sponsored transaction):
```ts
const result = await provider.request({
  method: 'wallet_sendCalls',
  params: [{
    version: '1.0',
    chainId: numberToHex(baseSepoliaChainId),
    from: user,
    calls,
    capabilities: {
      paymasterService: { url: paymasterServiceUrl }
    }
  }]
});
```

ERC20 PAYMASTERS specifics:
- pm_getPaymasterData request includes context { erc20: address }
- Response must include tokenPayment info: { tokenAddress, maxFee, decimals, name } on success or error with data.acceptedTokens on rejection.

Atomic capability
-----------------
- Check wallet_getCapabilities(account)['0x2105'].atomic.supported === 'supported'
- If supported and you set atomicRequired: true in wallet_sendCalls, wallet will execute batch atomically.
- Error codes: 4100 (unsupported), 5700 (atomic required but not supported), 5750 (atomic upgrade rejected)

AuxiliaryFunds (MagicSpend)
---------------------------
- capability auxiliaryFunds indicates wallet may access funds outside the on-chain balance (e.g., Coinbase balances).
- If supported, apps must not disable actions solely because on-chain balances are insufficient.
- Check via wallet_getCapabilities before deciding to disable UI.

FlowControl (ERC-7867 proposed)
-------------------------------
- Allows specifying onFailure behavior per call in batch (continue|stop|retry) and fallbackCall.
- Proposed behavior; not finalized. Use only with capability detection.

Sign & Verify Typed Data (EIP-712)
----------------------------------
- Use eth_signTypedData_v4 via provider.request({ method: 'eth_signTypedData_v4', params: [address, JSON.stringify(typedData)] })
- Verify server-side using viem.createPublicClient.verifyTypedData
- Note: For smart contract wallets, verification will account for ERC-1271 validation and ERC-6492 undeployed account wrappers.

Batch error handling (common)
-----------------------------
When calling wallet_sendCalls or batch APIs, handle:
- error.code === 4001 => user rejected
- error.code === 5740 => batch too large
- error.code === -32602 => invalid params
- Other codes are documented per method (5700, 5710, etc.)

Key SDK utilities & usage examples
---------------------------------
generateKeyPair / getKeypair:
```ts
import { generateKeyPair, getKeypair } from '@base-org/account';
let kp = await getKeypair();
if (!kp) kp = await generateKeyPair();
```

getCryptoKeyAccount:
```ts
import { getCryptoKeyAccount } from '@base-org/account';
const cryptoAccount = await getCryptoKeyAccount();
if (cryptoAccount?.account) {
  console.log(cryptoAccount.account.address);
}
```

Sub-account creation:
```ts
const sdk = createBaseAccountSDK({ appName: 'Demo', appChainIds: [84532] });
const provider = sdk.getProvider();
await provider.request({
  method: 'wallet_addSubAccount',
  params: [{ account: { type: 'create', keys: [{ type: 'p256', publicKey: '0x...' }] } }]
});
```

Spend permission flow:
```ts
import { requestSpendPermission, prepareSpendCallData } from '@base-org/account/spend-permission';
const permission = await requestSpendPermission({ account, spender, token, chainId, allowance: 1_000_000n, periodInDays: 30, provider });

const calls = await prepareSpendCallData({ permission, amount: 1000n });
// submit as batch from your spender account
await provider.request({ method: 'wallet_sendCalls', params: [{ version: '2.0', atomicRequired: true, from: spender, calls }] });
```

Basename resolution example (viem/minimal):
```ts
import { createPublicClient, http } from 'viem';
import { base } from 'viem/chains';
import L2ResolverAbi from '@/abis/L2ResolverAbi';
const client = createPublicClient({ chain: base, transport: http() });

const addressReverseNode = convertReverseNodeToBytes(address, base.id);
const basename = await client.readContract({ abi: L2ResolverAbi, address: BASENAME_L2_RESOLVER_ADDRESS, functionName: 'name', args: [addressReverseNode] });
```

Integration quickstarts (essentials)
-----------------------------------
Web (HTML + JS) minimal:
- Use CDN: <script src="https://unpkg.com/@base-org/account/dist/base-account.min.js"></script>
- Example: initialize provider: window.createBaseAccountSDK({ appName: 'Quickstart' }).getProvider();
- Use provider.request to sign in or window.base.pay to pay (CDN global exposes window.base helpers).

React Quickstart:
- npm install @base-org/account @base-org/account-ui
- createBaseAccountSDK in bundle or component and use getProvider() + UI components SignInWithBaseButton and BasePayButton.

Wagmi Quickstart:
- npm install wagmi viem @base-org/account
- Create createConfig with baseAccount connector and custom(provider) transport for Wagmi.

Privy Quickstart:
- npm add @privy-io/react-auth @privy-io/wagmi-connector wagmi viem @base-org/account
- Use PrivyProvider and WagmiProvider; configure embedded wallets, supported chains base, and add base_account in walletList.

Mobile (React Native) Quickstart:
- Install @mobile-wallet-protocol/client, polyfills expo-standard-web-crypto, react-native-url-polyfill, and set up EIP1193Provider with custom scheme myapp://

Telemetry
---------
- Default telemetry: enabled (opt-out). Configure via createBaseAccountSDK({ preference: { telemetry: false } })
- Telemetry events are anonymous, operational; do not include sensitive data or keys.

Brand & UI Guidelines (short)
-----------------------------
- Use official components for consistency.
- SignInWithBase button: Base blue square (always same shade), on dark backgrounds use white version. Text "Sign in with Base".
- BasePayButton uses combination mark; do not write "Base Pay" as text instead of mark.
- Follow brand assets and spacing requirements in docs.

Error codes & troubleshooting
-----------------------------
Common RPC error codes:
- 4001: user rejected request
- 4100: method not supported by wallet/provider
- 4200: wallet not available / disconnected
- 4900: disconnected
- 4902: unrecognized chain id (wallet_switchEthereumChain)
- -32602: invalid params
- -32601: method not found
- -32000: server error / execution reverted
- 5700: capability required but not supported
- 5740: batch too large
- 5750: capability upgrade rejected

Popup tips:
- Ensure popup opened by direct user click (avoid long synchronous logic between click and provider call).
- Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) header: use "same-origin-allow-popups" or "unsafe-none" to allow popup. "same-origin" will break popup flow.
- Popup linger: after a popup responds, it remains open for ~200ms to accept follow-up requests. If follow-up request happens outside this window, browser may block subsequent popup.

Gas usage & gasnotes
--------------------
- Smart contract wallet transactions cost more gas than EOA equivalents.
- Estimates (rough):
  - Native token transfer: EOA ~21k gas; Base Account ~100k gas
  - ERC-20 transfer: EOA ~65k gas; Base Account ~150k gas
  - First deployment of account: ~300k+ gas

Unsupported calls or limitations
--------------------------------
- Self-calls (dapps calling user's own smart account address) are disallowed for security.
- CREATE opcode: unsupported for smart account deployments in certain flows (use CREATE2 or factories).
- Solidity transfer built-in may fail for Base Accounts (WETH9 unwrapping may use transfer -> failure); avoid relying on transfer to send ETH to smart wallets.

Complete method reference highlights
-----------------------------------
(See provider methods listing above in "Provider RPC methods".) Each method has request param shape, return shape, and common error conditions noted earlier. For code examples, reference the "Selected request/response examples" section.

Best practices & security
-------------------------
- Always verify signatures server-side (viem verifyMessage / verifyTypedData).
- Generate fresh nonces for SIWE; track used nonces server-side to prevent replay.
- Check wallet capabilities (wallet_getCapabilities) before relying on advanced features (atomic, paymaster, auxiliaryFunds, dataCallback).
- Use HTTPS for callback URLs; ngrok for local dev.
- Avoid relying solely on on-chain balance if auxiliaryFunds is supported.
- Add robust server-side validation for dataCallback flows.
- Handle popup blocking by keeping provider requests directly tied to user click handlers.

Example: End-to-end Sign-in with Base using Wagmi + Backend:
```ts
// Client (React + Wagmi)
const baseConnector = connectors.find(c => c.id === 'baseAccountWallet');
await connectAsync({ connector: baseConnector }); // Wagmi connect
const provider = baseConnector.provider;
const nonce = await fetch('/auth/nonce').then(r => r.text());
const authResult = await provider.request({ method: 'wallet_connect', params: [{ version: '1', capabilities: { signInWithEthereum: { nonce, chainId: '0x2105' } } }] });
const { address } = authResult.accounts[0];
const { message, signature } = authResult.accounts[0].capabilities.signInWithEthereum;
await fetch('/auth/verify', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ address, message, signature }) });

// Server (Express + Viem)
app.get('/auth/nonce', (req,res) => { const nonce = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex'); nonces.add(nonce); res.send(nonce); });
app.post('/auth/verify', async (req,res) => {
  const { address, message, signature } = req.body;
  const valid = await client.verifyMessage({ address, message, signature });
  if (!valid) return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid signature' });
  // create session
  res.json({ ok: true });
});
```

Examples & demos repository pointers
-----------------------------------
- Basenames resolver ABI gist: referenced in docs (L2ResolverAbi)
- Complete code examples: various gists linked in the source docs (basenames.tsx etc.)
- Demos: repos (coin-your-joke, onchain-vibes-store, sub-account-demo) exist in github.com/base/demos

Troubleshooting checklist
-------------------------
- If wallet popup shows spinner/error: check COOP header (same-origin-allow-popups) and popup being opened by click.
- If wallet methods return method_not_supported: fallback to eth_requestAccounts + personal_sign for older wallets.
- If pay() fails: ensure testnet flag matches for both pay() and getPaymentStatus; confirm user has USDC on appropriate chain or paymaster supports sponsorship.
- If batch fails: check batch size (5740), atomic capability, paymaster support if used.

Appendix: Selected provider request examples (quick reference)
--------------------------------------------------------------
- eth_requestAccounts -> params: []
- eth_accounts -> params: []
- wallet_connect -> params: [ { version?: string, capabilities?: {...} } ]
- wallet_getCapabilities -> params: [accountAddress]
- wallet_sendCalls -> params: [ {version:'2.0.0', id?:string, from, chainId, atomicRequired:boolean, calls:[{to,value,data}], capabilities?:{ paymasterService?:{url}, dataCallback?:{requests,callbackURL}} } ]
- wallet_getCallsStatus -> params: [callsId]
- wallet_addSubAccount -> params: [ { account: { type:'create'|'deployed', keys?:[], address?:string, chainId?:number } } ]
- wallet_getSubAccounts -> params: [ { account: address, domain: origin } ]
- personal_sign -> params: [dataHex, address]
- eth_signTypedData_v4 -> params: [address, JSON.stringify(typedData)]
- eth_sendTransaction -> params: [ txObject ]
- eth_sendRawTransaction -> params: [ signedTxHex ]
- wallet_addEthereumChain -> params: [ chainData ]
- wallet_switchEthereumChain -> params: [ { chainId: '0x...' } ]
- wallet_watchAsset -> params: { type:'ERC20', options: { address, symbol, decimals, image? } }

Final notes
-----------
This combined reference preserves code examples, signatures, type shapes, configurations, error handling guidance, integration recipes, and best practices across the Base Account documentation set. For implementation use the SDK packages:
- @base-org/account (core SDK)
- @base-org/account-ui/react (UI components)
- wagmi + viem for advanced integrations
- @privy-io/react-auth for Privy integration
- @mobile-wallet-protocol/client for React Native

For latest contract ABIs (basenames resolver, spend-permissions, smart-wallet), check the linked GitHub repos referenced in the original docs:
- https://github.com/base/basenames
- https://github.com/coinbase/smart-wallet
- https://github.com/coinbase/spend-permissions
